Plot the overlaps of the gene lists

Source: R/plotIntersect.R
plotIntersect.Rd

plotIntersect() draws an UpSet plot of the gene lists of sc.filter() with UpSetR::upset(), which needs the suggested package UpSetR, or returns its data.

plotIntersect(
  scmpObj,
  min_intersection_size = 1,
  keep_empty_groups = FALSE,
  width_ratio = 0.1,
  show_sets_size = FALSE,
  return = FALSE
)

Arguments

scmpObj

A ScMaSigPro object.

min_intersection_size

The smallest intersection drawn.

keep_empty_groups

Whether to draw the empty intersections.

width_ratio

Not used.

show_sets_size

Not used.

return

Whether to return the data instead of the plot.

Value

An upset object of UpSetR or, with return = TRUE, a data frame with one row per gene and a 0/1 column per gene list.

References

Conway JR, Lex A, Gehlenborg N (2017). UpSetR: an R package for the visualization of intersecting sets and their properties. Bioinformatics 33(18), 2938-2940. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btx364

See also

Other plots: plotBinTile(), plotDiagnostics(), plotTrend(), plotTrendCluster()

Author

Priyansh Srivastava spriyansh29@gmail.com

Examples

data("scmp.ob", package = "scMaSigPro")
# The genes of each list as 0/1 columns
head(plotIntersect(scmp.ob, return = TRUE))
#>        Path2vsPath1 Path1
#> Gene2             1     0
#> Gene3             1     1
#> Gene4             1     0
#> Gene9             1     1
#> Gene10            1     1
#> Gene15            1     1
if (requireNamespace("UpSetR", quietly = TRUE)) {
    plotIntersect(scmp.ob)
}
